headline: Network and generative models of AML treatment response and drug design
label: Aml Computational Modeling Frameworks
summary: Recent preprints and a published method apply explicit network and generative models to AML treatment and drug design.
synthesis: The dominant thread is an explicit computational model serving as the inferential core for therapeutic questions. Two AML preprints apply this to treatment and drug design: an edge-weighted digraph framework models cytarabine treatment contextuality and explores SAMHD1 inhibitors, with a web-based interface, while a metaheuristic fragment-assembly pipeline generates ligands against AlphaFold3-modeled, WGCNA-prioritized biomarkers and tests them by docking. The published gMIS work is not AML-specific. It extends minimal intervention set formulations from gMCS to knockouts and knock-ins across integrated metabolic-regulatory networks. What is new across the set is that the model structure itself, rather than only its output, becomes the analytical object.
